arxiv-2005-05261.title: A modular extension for a computer algebra system
arxiv-2005-05261.creator: Migran N. Gevorkyan, Anna V. Korolkova, Dmitry S. Kulyabov, Leonid A. Sevastianov
arxiv-2005-05261.description: Abstract Computer algebra systems are complex software systems that cover a wide range of scientific and practical problems. However, the absolute coverage cannot be achieved. Often, it is required to create a user extension for an existing computer algebra system. In this case, the extensibility of the system should be taken into account.

arxiv-2108-00028.title: Extended particle absorber for efficient modeling of intense laser-solid interactions
arxiv-2108-00028.creator: Kyle G. Miller, Joshua May, Frederico Fiuza, Warren B. Mori
arxiv-2108-00028.description: Abstract An extended thermal particle boundary condition is devised to more efficiently and accurately model laser-plasma interactions in overdense plasmas. Particle-in-cell simulations of such interactions require many particles per cell, and a large region of background plasma is often necessary to correctly mimic a semi-infinite plasma and avoid electron refluxing from a truncated plasma.

arxiv-2205-11709.title: Hardware/Software Co-Assurance using the Rust Programming Language and ACL2
arxiv-2205-11709.creator: David Hardin
arxiv-2205-11709.description: Abstract The Rust programming language has garnered significant interest and use as a modern, type-safe, memory-safe, and potentially formally analyzable programming language. Our interest in Rust stems from its potential as a hardware/software co-assurance language, with application to critical systems such as autonomous vehicles. We report on the first known use of Rust as a High-Level Synthesis (HLS) language.

arxiv-2310-12233.title: Generalized time-reversal symmetry and effective theories for nonequilibrium matter
arxiv-2310-12233.creator: Xiaoyang Huang, Jack H. Farrell, Aaron J. Friedman, Isabella Zane, Paolo Glorioso, Andrew Lucas
arxiv-2310-12233.description: Abstract The past decade has witnessed the development of systematic effective theories for dissipative thermal systems. Here, we describe an analogous effective theory framework that applies to the classical stochastic dynamics of nonequilibrium systems. We illustrate this approach using a range of examples, including nonreciprocal (predator-prey) dynamics, dissipative and driven rigid-body motion, and active chiral fluids and solids.

arxiv-2408-10565.title: Impurities induced vortex lattice melting and turbulence in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates
arxiv-2408-10565.creator: Rony Boral, Swarup K. Sarkar, Paulsamy Muruganandam, Pankaj K. Mishra
arxiv-2408-10565.description: Abstract We investigate the impact of various impurities on rotating Bose-Einstein condensates confined within two-dimensional harmonic and optical lattice potentials. Without impurities, the rotating condensates display an organized square lattice pattern of vortices due to the influence of a square optical lattice.

arxiv-2408-15834.title: Characterization of dynamical systems with scanty data using Persistent Homology and Machine Learning
arxiv-2408-15834.creator: Rishab Antosh, Sanjit Das, N. Nirmal Thyagu
arxiv-2408-15834.description: Abstract Determination of the nature of the dynamical state of a system as a function of its parameters is an important problem in the study of dynamical systems. This problem becomes harder in experimental systems where the obtained data is inadequate (low-res) or has missing values.

arxiv-2507-06551.title: A Family of Block-Centered Schemes for Contaminant Transport Equations with Adsorption via Integral Method with Variational Limit
arxiv-2507-06551.creator: He Liu, Xiongbo Zheng, Xiaole Li, Mingze Ji
arxiv-2507-06551.description: Abstract This paper develops a class of high-order conservative schemes for contaminant transport with equilibrium adsorption, based on the Integral Method with Variational Limit on block-centered grids. By incorporating four parameters, the scheme can reproduce classical fourth-order compact schemes and further extend to sixth- and eighth-order accurate formulations, all within a unified framework.

arxiv-2510-18053.title: Adaptive Divergence Regularized Policy Optimization for Fine-tuning Generative Models
arxiv-2510-18053.creator: Jiajun Fan, Tong Wei, Chaoran Cheng, Yuxin Chen, Ge Liu
arxiv-2510-18053.description: Abstract Balancing exploration and exploitation during reinforcement learning fine-tuning of generative models presents a critical challenge, as existing approaches rely on fixed divergence regularization that creates an inherent dilemma: strong regularization preserves model capabilities but limits reward optimization, while weak regularization enables greater alignment but risks instability or reward hacking.

It is based on the notion that the brain is an inference machine that actively constructs hypotheses to explain or predict its sensations. This perspective provides a normative (Bayes-optimal)...

pmc-10505043.title: Atraumatic Spontaneous Splenic Rupture With Unknown Etiology
pmc-10505043.creator: Humberto Perez, Han Sol Jeong, Jason Smith DO
pmc-10505043.description: Splenic rupture of all causes is a potentially life-threatening event for patients. The infrequency of atraumatic splenic rupture (ASR) poses a significant diagnostic challenge due to atypical findings. ASR is commonly due to a spleen with an underlying disease process such as malignancy, infection, coagulopathies, or neoplasms. However, ASR without an identifiable cause is rare and poses further complexity.

pmc-10638738.title: Effects of life-sustaining treatment plans on healthcare expenditure and healthcare utilization
pmc-10638738.creator: Wonjeong Jeong, Selin Kim, Hyunkyu Kim, Eun-Cheol Park, Sung-In Jang
pmc-10638738.description: PurposeTo develop an ethical and cultural infrastructure for Life-Sustaining Treatment (LST) plan, it is crucial to carefully analyze its impact and ensure that healthcare utilization is maintained at an appropriate level, avoiding excessive medical interventions. This study aims to investigate the effects of LST decisions on both healthcare expenditure and utilization.

pmc-10650130.title: Effect of Bioactive Compounds from Pumpkin Powder on the Quality and Textural Properties of Shortbread Cookies
pmc-10650130.creator: Aliona Ghendov-Mosanu, Natalia Netreba, Greta Balan, Daniela Cojocari, Olga Boestean, Viorica Bulgaru, Angela Gurev, Liliana Popescu, Olga Deseatnicova, Vladislav Resitca, Carmen Socaciu, Adela Pintea, Tamar Sanikidze, Rodica Sturza, Vincenzo Lo Turco, Angela Giorgia Potorti
pmc-10650130.description: The problem of food with functional ingredients, characterized by low energy intake and a variety of phytonutrients with biological activity, is one of the concerns of the population. The objectives of this study were to investigate the effect of pumpkin powder and its bioactive components on the quality, color and textural properties of shortbread cookies.

pmc-10651638.title: Reconsideration of the current models of estimated kidney function‐based drug dose adjustment in older adults: The role of biological age
pmc-10651638.creator: Radin Alikhani, Manjunath P Pai
pmc-10651638.description: Human lifespan has increased from a median of 46.5 years in 1950 to 71.7 years in 2022. As people age, one of the inevitable consequences is a decline in kidney function and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) which can have direct or indirect effects on the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles of many drugs.

pmc-11650548.title: Cephalic ganglia transcriptomics of the American cockroach Periplaneta americana (Blattodea: Blattidae)
pmc-11650548.creator: Ilana Levy, Ryan Arvidson
pmc-11650548.description: The American cockroach Periplaneta americana (L.) (Blattodea, Blattidae) has been a model organism for biochemical and physiological study for almost a century, however, its use does not benefit from the genetic tools found in key model species such as Drosophila melanogaster.

pmc-12564282.title: Ultrasensitive Electrochemical Immunoassays of IgG and CA125 Based on Glucose Oxidase-Catalyzed Signal Amplification with Gold Staining
pmc-12564282.creator: Long Chao, Zhisong Wu, Shiqiang Qi, Aigui Xu, Zhao Huang, Dexuan Yan
pmc-12564282.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Herein, we propose an ultrasensitive electrochemical immunosensor based on glucose oxidase labeling and enzyme-catalyzed Au staining. In brief, the primary antibody (Ab1), bovine serum albumin, an antigen and then a bionanocomposite that contains a second antibody (Ab2), poly(3-anilineboronic acid) (PABA), Au nanoparticles (AuNPs) and glucose oxidase (GOx) are modified on a glassy carbon electrode coated with multiwalled carbon nanotubes, yielding a corresponding sandwich-type immunoelectrode.

pmc-13323572.title: Association of Subclinical Cardiac Remodeling With Incident Cancer in the MESA Cohort
pmc-13323572.creator: Xinjiang Cai, Quinn White, Jordan Juarez, Omar Chehab, Bharath Ambale‐Venkatesh, W Craig Johnson, Spencer L Hansen, Kosuke Inoue, Joao AC Lima, Karol E Watson, Robyn L McClelland
pmc-13323572.description: BackgroundPatients with established cardiovascular disease have an increased risk of cancer; however, the association between subclinical cardiac remodeling and cancer development remains unclear. We aimed to examine the association between cardiac magnetic resonance imaging–derived measures of subclinical cardiac remodeling and incident cancer in the MESA (Multi‐Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) cohort.

pmc-13379409.title: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) as a surrogate outcome measure for GM2 gangliosidoses
pmc-13379409.creator: Kyriakos Martakis, Nicolas J. Abreu, Joshua J. Baker, Peter R. Baker II, Ian Billington, T. Andrew Burrow, Mallory Factor, Taylor Fields, Cassandra Fields, Jennifer L. Gannon, Megan Grosso, Jorgji Kerthi, Marc C. Patterson, Brian J. Shayota, Michael Strupp, Lennard Strupp, Tatiana Bremova-Ert
pmc-13379409.description: BackgroundThe GM2 gangliosidoses (GM2) are ultra-rare neurodegenerative disorders caused by deficient hexosaminidase A and/or B activity, leading to lysosomal GM2 ganglioside accumulation. Disease onset ranges from infancy to adulthood, with earlier onset associated with more rapid progression. Neurofilament light chain (NfL), a sensitive marker of axonal injury, has been extensively investigated as a biomarker for neurodegenerative disorders, including GM2.

pmc-13592035.title: Snacking behaviors and early childhood caries severity among Myanmar preschool children: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13592035.creator: Phue Wai Han, Kaung Myat Thwin, Wa Than Lin, Natcha Tassanapong, Sachiko Takehara, Hiroshi Ogawa
pmc-13592035.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEarly childhood caries (ECC) is highly prevalent among preschool children, particularly in Southeast Asian countries. Although dietary intake is a well-established risk factor, evidence on how specific snacking behaviors contribute to caries severity remains limited.

uslaw-usc-t16-s1338.title: 16 U.S.C. § 1338 — Criminal provisions
uslaw-usc-t16-s1338.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s1338.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 30 (Wild Horses And Burros: Protection, Management, And Control). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Violations; penalties; trial Any person who— (1) willfully removes or attempts to remove a wild free-roaming horse or burro from the public lands, without authority from the Secretary, or (2) converts a wild free-roaming horse or burro to private use.
